thread:
maya: heads-up: saw host->gpu churn on small-embed tenants. thinking about a reservoir-style prefetch quota so tenants get a limited burst budget instead of global aggressive prefetch.

alex: sounds useful. how does reservoir differ from simple max_bucket cap?

maya: cap is static. reservoir refills over time and lets short bursts spike to aggressive prefetch, then drains. smoother across mixed workloads.

orin: nice. refill rate could be proportional to tenant SLA class. e.g., gold gets 5 tokens/sec, silver 2, bronze 0.5. token spend is per-page prefetch weight.

jeff: need to account for fragmentation: prefetching many tiny pages can bloat host mmapped regions and cause evict thrash. reservoir should cost more for small non-contig pages.

sara: agree. add page_weight = ceil(page_bytes / 64KB). small pages heavier relative to benefit. also prefer coalesced regions when possible.

maya: runtime interface idea: alloc_hint { prefetch_policy: reservoir, weight: X, granularity: page|segment, prefer_coalesce: true }

orin: implementation note: offload-controller tracks reservoir per-tenant+node. when a batch arrives, controller computes token budget for that batch and returns a per-allocation allowance.

jeff: batch merging problem again. multiple requests in same batch from different tenants -> controller needs to atomically allocate per-tenant tokens. should be ok as long as we return per-alloc decisions rather than a single batch-wide mode.

sara: but continuous batching means allocations may interleave. cheapest approach: controller returns an allowance map for each alloc request id. allocator consults map and issues prefetch only if allowed.

maya: on telemetry: emit PrefetchReservoirEvent sampled at 0.5% with fields [tenant, alloc_id, tokens_before, tokens_after, pages_prefetched, bytes]. keep proto tiny (string ids + ints).

perf-bot: micro-run results: basic reservoir (gold:5/s, silver:2/s) reduced sustained bandwidth by 28% and kept p99 within 5% for mixed traffic. downside: short p99 spikes when refill exhausted.

orin: maybe add emergency-probe: if p99 spikes and reservoir drained, allow transient overdraft up to X tokens but billable and throttled per-cluster safety.

jeff: policy knobs: max_overdraft_per_tenant, overdraft_penalty_multiplier (for billing), cluster_safety_toggle. Document semantics.

sara: eviction interplay: allocator should mark prefetched pages with a soft-resident flag so evictor considers guest locality when compacting. otherwise we'll evict the pages we just prefetch.

maya: agree. make prefetched pages set eviction_priority lower (i.e., prefer to keep) for short time window T after prefetch. also decrease keep-time if reservoir budget is low.

orin: can implement as TTL-based boost: on prefetch set boost_until = now + min(T_default, tokens_left * per_token_ttl).

jeff: safety: simulate tenant storms with perf harness. and add a per-node global bandwidth gate so aggregate prefetch can't saturate PCIe.

maya: next steps: 1) prototype controller tokens + allocator hook (orin), 2) perf harness scenarios + telemetry (sara + perf), 3) console UI for refill rates and overdraft controls (product), 4) RFC doc summarizing API and eviction interactions (alex).

alex: please include an example YAML for tenant config in RFC. e.g.:
```
tenant_config:
  prefetch:
    policy: reservoir
    refill_rate: 2 # tokens/sec
    max_overdraft: 10
    prefer_coalesce: true
```

maya: also add note: interaction with quantized kernel memory layout (page packing) — maybe treat packed regions as single unit for weight. will investigate.

jeff: ack. include billing implications and a safety kill switch per-cluster.

orin: I'll start the offload-controller sketch and ping for design review.

maya: thanks all. I'll kick perf runs once prototype lands. :rocket:
